paragraphs: Rav Huna, father of Zeira the priest, and Abba B.B.Ch. were sitting and eating, while Rabbi Zeira stood and served them. Abba B.B.Ch. said to him, “What, are your hands cut off …?” Rav Huna became angry and told him, “Is it not enough that you sit while he stands? Moreover, he is a priest, and it is forbidden to make use of a priest.” Yefeh Mareh explains there that Rav Huna, Zeira’s father, grew angry at Rabbi Abba B.B.Ch., who was shaming Zeira, a priest: Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot chapter 8, halakhah 5. Thus this Rav Huna is not the unqualified Rav Huna, who was not a priest, as stated in Gittin 59b: Rav Huna read in the priest’s place—Rashi explains that he was an Israelite—because Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi, distinguished priests of the Land of Israel, deferred to him (see above, Rav Huna). There in Yefeh Mareh, in a gloss from the eminent teacher Mikhel, of blessed memory: Tosafot disputes whether a priest can waive his honor. Rabbi Zeira’s serving before them implies that he can waive it: Zeira’s father did not object because it was disrespectful to use his services against his will, but because of the words to his son, “Are your hands cut off?” One cannot say that a priest can never waive his honor, and here it was different because of Rav Huna’s honor, since he read in the priest’s place as the greatest of the generation, and they therefore let him serve him. This is not so, for there the reason … . Thus according to his explanation, this Zeira the priest was Abba B.B.Ch.’s son, and this Rav Huna was the unqualified one, an Israelite who read in the priest’s place. But this requires examination: we have not found Abba B.B.Ch. to have been a priest. In the end there is no decision whether Zeira the priest was Rav Huna’s son, as Yefeh Mareh explains, or Abba B.B.Ch.’s son. Yet I labored and found in Yalkut, end of Nechemyah, as follows: Abba and Rav Huna sat, and Zeira served. He carried wine and oil in one hand. Rav Huna said to him, “Is your other hand cut off?” Abba grew angry with him and said, “Is it not enough …? Moreover, he is a priest.” Thus Zeira was Abba’s son, and this Rav Huna was not a priest. It does not read bar bar Chana. Perhaps this Rabbi Abba was the son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, who was a priest. Thus Yalkut’s reading is the reverse of the Jerusalem Talmud’s.
